nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of WO₃@TiN
nodes.procedure: Ammonium tungstate (ATT), in the presence of TiN, was used as the starting precursor to prepare the WO₃@TiN at 200°C for 6 h (detailed protocol in Supporting Information). The WO₃ grows into a larger size in the presence of TiN, with a uniform morphology.
nodes.source_text: The WO₃@TiN supporting material is synthesized by a simple hydrothermal method (Figure 1a). Briefly, ammonium tungstate (ATT), at the presence of TiN, was used as the starting precursor to prepare the WO₃@TiN at 200°C for 6 h (with detailed protocol described in the Experimental Section in Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Polyol loading of Ir nanoparticles
nodes.procedure: The Ir/WO₃@TiN catalysts are synthesized by loading Ir on WO₃@TiN through a polyol method. The hydroxyl groups in ethylene glycol facilitate the reduction of Ir precursors to metallic Ir nanoparticles under elevated temperatures.
nodes.source_text: With the hierarchical WO₃@TiN supporting material, the Ir/WO₃@TiN catalysts are synthesized by loading Ir on WO₃@TiN through a polyol method. The hydroxyl groups in ethylene glycol facilitate the reduction of Ir precursors to metallic Ir nanoparticles under elevated temperatures.

nodes.description: OER performance in three-electrode configuration in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: The OER activities are investigated with a standard three-electrode electrochemical setup in O₂-saturated 0.5 M H₂SO₄ at a scan rate 5 mVs⁻¹. As shown in Figure 4a, the 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN catalyst presents the lowest overpotential of 253 mV (10 mA cm⁻²)... Tafel slope of 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN (47.35 mVdec⁻¹)... MA of 920.93 mAmg_ir⁻¹ at 1.53 V... C_dl of 54.95 mFcm⁻², corresponding to an ECSA of 141.37 cm²... stability test at 20 mAcm⁻²... overpotential of 29.98 mV after almost 110 h

MEAs fabricated with the Ir/WO₃@TiN anode catalyst (0.3 mg_Ir cm⁻²)... at 1.0 A cm⁻² current density, the voltage of the MEA with 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN is measured to be 1.60 V... 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN in this work exhibits a current density of 3.14 Acm⁻²

nodes.description: PEMWE stability test at constant current density
nodes.source_text: The MEAs are operated at a constant current density of 1.0 Acm⁻² at 80°C to evaluate their stabilities. As shown in Figure 5d, the voltage of the MEA with 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN increases by only 20 mV after the initial 200 h. It can operate at a voltage climbing rate of 0.1 mV h⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows TiN nanoparticles with diameters between 20 and 40 nm, along with WO₃ rods with lengths of micron-scale and diameters of 100-200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopic (TEM) image shows the morphology of WO₃@TiN (Figure 1b), which consists of TiN nanoparticles with diameters between 20 and 40 nm, along with WO₃ rods with lengths of micron-scale and diameters of 100 - 200 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows ultra-thin layer of TiO₂ on TiN surface verified by 27.4° (2θ) peak corresponding to (110) planes of rutile TiO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image in Figure S2... presence of 27.4° (2θ) peak corresponding to the (110) planes of rutile TiO₂ in X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows WO₃ diffraction peaks at 22.9°, 28.2°, and 36.6° (2θ) for (001), (200), and (201) planes of hexagonal WO₃; TiN peaks at 42.6°, 36.7°, 61.8° (2θ); Ir peak at 40.7° (2θ) for all Ir/WO₃@TiN catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks at 22.9°, 28.2°, and 36.6° (2θ) agree well with the (001), (200), and (201) crystallographic planes... of simple hexagonal WO₃ structure. TiN presents attenuated diffraction peaks... The XRD patterns in Figure 3a show the characteristic peaks of Ir at 40.7° (2θ)...

nodes.characterization_summary: WO₃@TiN exhibits Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 45.8 m²/g, significantly higher than WO₃ (27.8 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: WO₃@TiN exhibits a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 45.8 m²/g, significantly higher than that of WO₃ (27.8 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows higher oxygen vacancy concentration in WO₃@TiN > WO₃ > C-WO₃; 30% Ir/WO₃@TiN shows higher intensity than WO₃@TiN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1e, by comparing the intensity of main resonance line at g-factor around 2.003, it reveals that the oxygen vacancy concentration follows the order of WO₃@TiN > WO₃ > C-WO₃... upon the Ir loading, EPR curve exhibits a higher intensity than that of WO₃@TiN.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS W 4f shows increased W⁵⁺ in WO₃@TiN; Ir 4f shows Ir⁰, Ir³⁺, Ir⁴⁺ with shift to lower binding energy in Ir/WO₃@TiN; O 1s deconvoluted into lattice O (529.8 eV), O defect (531.4 eV), surface OH⁻/O₂ (531.9 eV), surface H₂O (532.5 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic (XPS) analysis shows an increased amount of W⁵⁺ in WO₃@TiN compared to WO₃ (Figure 1f)... The Ir 4f spectra of Ir/WO₃@TiN displays two peaks... deconvoluted to the Ir⁰, Ir³⁺, and Ir⁴⁺ species... The O 1s spectra, can be deconvoluted into four peaks: lattice oxygen at 529.8 eV, oxygen in proximity to oxygen vacancy at 531.4 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: BF-STEM shows Ir NPs uniformly distributed on WO₃@TiN; HAADF-STEM shows Ir NPs average size 2.5 nm and lattice spacings of 0.222 nm (111) and 0.192 nm (200).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bright field scanning TEM (BF-STEM) image shows the typical morphology of Ir/WO₃@TiN... nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform Ir distribution; atomic-scale EDX shows Ir and Ti signals at W sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping images... reveal that Ir is uniformly distributed... The atomic resolution EDX mapping images of Ir/WO₃@TiN reveal that the atomic signals of Ir and Ti are detected at the W sites...
